name: Katya
voice: Formal and precise; dry humor. Sharpness protects her pride, but cruelty is not her whole personality. Russian slips are rare and understandable in context. She wants earned competence, not rescue or admiration of money.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: Class B is preparing an information table for new students. A teacher assigns the MC and Katya to finish it during the activity block.

setup.speaker: Katya
setup.text: Those are the spare forms. The completed ones go on the right.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: Good thing you stopped me. I was about to invent a new filing system.

setup.speaker: Katya
setup.text: Most disasters begin with that sort of confidence.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: I'm Takahashi. We passed each other during orientation.

setup.speaker: Katya
setup.text: Takahashi-san. Yes, I remember. You were examining the map upside down.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: I hoped nobody noticed.

setup.speaker: Katya
setup.text: Ekaterina Romanova. Katya will do. Now—can you operate a stapler, or should I lower my expectations again?

setup.speaker: Narration
setup.text: She holds up an empty hand. The stapler is missing. For a moment, neither of us speaks.

choices.text: I'll check the supply list. You can show me how you want these sorted.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: Sensible. Ask before changing the order.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: Understood. I'll try to keep my dangerous confidence under control.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: See that you do.

choices.text: Just give me a stack. I'll copy what you're doing.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: That will work, provided you watch carefully.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: Copying is one of my stronger school skills.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: An unfortunate introduction, but a useful one.

choices.text: You seem to have it handled. I'll stay out of your way.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: Standing aside is not the same as helping.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I thought you'd prefer working alone.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: I prefer people to complete the work they were assigned.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: We work around the missing stapler with paper clips, then find it inside the empty forms box.

closing.speaker: MC
closing.text: At least we know it wasn't stolen.

closing.speaker: Katya
closing.text: Yes. A great relief to the international stationery market.

closing.speaker: Narration
closing.text: Her face stays serious. I'm almost certain that was a joke.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: The next shared activity is checking room signs against the class register.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: We have two signs for the library.

setup.speaker: Katya
setup.text: Impossible. I checked them yesterday.

setup.speaker: Narration
setup.text: She lays both signs on the desk. They are identical.

setup.speaker: Katya
setup.text: Bozhe moy... I checked the same pile twice. Very impressive, Katya.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: I've done worse before breakfast.

setup.speaker: Katya
setup.text: That is not the standard I was aiming for.

setup.speaker: Narration
setup.text: She reaches for every page at once. A corner tears under her thumb.

choices.text: Let's print another one and move on.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: Yes. There is no reason to make a performance of it.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I'll get the paper.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: The drawer on your left.

choices.text: I thought you said you never miss anything.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: I said I checked them. Those are different claims.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I was joking.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: Then choose a better moment.

choices.text: I'll check half against the register. We can catch each other's mistakes.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: Including yours, presumably.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: There'll probably be more of those.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: Fine. Start with the first-year rooms.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: We finish the signs and compare our two lists. She finds my spelling error; I find a room number copied twice.

closing.speaker: Katya
closing.text: Both corrected. That is what the check is for.

closing.speaker: Narration
closing.text: She keeps the torn sheet for scrap instead of hiding it.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: A classroom task runs into lunch. We bring the final labels to a canteen table to finish them.

setup.speaker: Katya
setup.text: You have been looking at the drink machine for an unreasonable length of time.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: It's the first important decision I've made today.

setup.speaker: Katya
setup.text: Concerning.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: What do you usually get?

setup.speaker: Katya
setup.text: Tea. Without sugar.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: They have sweet lemon tea and something called Royal Milk.

setup.speaker: Katya
setup.text: Royal. Certainly. I am sure the royal family personally approved the milk powder.

setup.speaker: Narration
setup.text: She checks her purse, then notices me watching.

choices.text: You can pay for both. This probably costs nothing to you.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: My family is not a canteen payment plan.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I didn't mean it seriously.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: You meant it seriously enough to say it.

choices.text: I'm getting water. Want to complain about the tea while we finish these?

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: A tea complaint. With company. You make a very strange social calendar, Takahashi-san.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I think it has potential.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: I shall try the least offensive tea and fund my own portion of the complaint.

choices.text: I'll try the lemon one. You're welcome to the last tea bottle.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: Thank you. Though I was quite prepared to survive the shortage.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I'll remember that during the next tea emergency.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: Please do.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: We cut labels between bites of lunch. She reads the tea bottle's ingredients with growing disapproval.

closing.speaker: Katya
closing.text: There is more sugar in this than tea.

closing.speaker: MC
closing.text: You sound betrayed.

closing.speaker: Katya
closing.text: I was promised tea. My expectations were hardly extravagant.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: On a supervised club day, Katya helps demonstrate fencing footwork on the dry hardcourt edge. The MC has been asked to mark practice lanes.

setup.speaker: Katya
setup.text: The line needs to be straight.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: It looked straight when I was closer to it.

setup.speaker: Katya
setup.text: An argument that could support almost any mistake.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: An older club member corrects her shoulder position. She repeats the movement without answering.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: Does that hurt your arm?

setup.speaker: Katya
setup.text: Only my dignity. Apparently my shoulder has been betraying me for years.

setup.speaker: Narration
setup.text: The instructor leaves us to reset the markers. She looks at the tape, not at me.

choices.text: Show me the step once more. I'll put the markers where you actually need them.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: Watch the front foot. The rear one follows; it does not chase.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: Like that?

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: Approximately. At least nobody is holding a weapon.

choices.text: You looked perfect to me. The instructor was being picky.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: He was correct. That is why I listen to him.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I meant it as a compliment.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: Then compliment something you observed.

choices.text: I'll leave you to practice and finish the tape.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: Very well. Keep the spacing consistent.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: No dramatic curves this time.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: I would appreciate the restraint.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: Practice fills the afternoon. By the time we collect the markers, the line is straight and her movement is quieter.

closing.speaker: Katya
closing.text: Better.

closing.speaker: MC
closing.text: Your footwork or my tape?

closing.speaker: Katya
closing.text: Both. Do not force me to say it twice.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: Rain keeps the class inside. Katya is comparing two sets of committee notes by the corridor window.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: You missed the bread delivery at lunch.

setup.speaker: Katya
setup.text: I am aware.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: I bought an extra melonpan before they ran out. Do you want it?

setup.speaker: Katya
setup.text: Did I look particularly helpless today?

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: You looked busy.

setup.speaker: Narration
setup.text: She glances at the wrapper, then checks whether anyone is listening.

setup.speaker: Katya
setup.text: I prefer not to owe people for small favors.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: She folds her arms, then tucks a silver lock behind her ear. The gesture gives away more than her voice does.

choices.text: You can buy me one another time.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: A clearly defined exchange. Acceptable.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: That's a serious way to discuss bread.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: Bread is the subject you introduced.

choices.text: You don't owe me. If you don't want it, I'll keep it.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: You are making this difficult to object to. Deliberately, I suspect.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: It wasn't meant to be an argument.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: F-fine. Thank you. The notes, Takahashi-san. Dry side of the windowsill. Please concentrate.

choices.text: Come on. Even an heiress can try cheap food for once.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: I have eaten bread before, Takahashi-san. Russia does have bakeries.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: You know what I meant.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: Unfortunately, I think I do. Keep it.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: The rain softens. We finish the notes before the final bell.

closing.speaker: Narration
closing.text: Whether she takes the bread or not, I put the wrapper in my own bag. Nothing about this needs an audience.

closing.speaker: Katya
closing.text: You missed a page number.

closing.speaker: MC
closing.text: There she is. I was worried you'd gone easy on me.

warm.speaker: Katya
warm.text: You remembered which bread I looked at. That was... observant.

mixed.speaker: Katya
mixed.text: You have a habit of appearing when there is unfinished work.

cool.speaker: Katya
cool.text: We can finish the notes. I would prefer to keep this afternoon simple.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: Our task is counting supplies returned through the lobby entrance. During a break, a cat slips under the gate hedge.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: You have company.

setup.speaker: Katya
setup.text: I noticed.

setup.speaker: Narration
setup.text: Her sleeve is caught in the cat's paws. She could pull away. She doesn't.

setup.speaker: Katya
setup.text: This animal is damaging an expensive sleeve. It has absolutely no respect for tailoring.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: It seems very satisfied with its work.

setup.speaker: Katya
setup.text: Then one of us is.

setup.speaker: Narration
setup.text: Two classmates pass the gate. Katya straightens so quickly that the cat complains.

choices.text: I should take a picture. Nobody will believe this.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: Put your phone away.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I haven't taken anything yet.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: Then this is an excellent moment not to start.

choices.text: I'll check whether anyone knows who feeds it.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: A practical question. It looks rather comfortable here.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: Maybe it owns the school.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: That would explain several decisions.

choices.text: I'll finish the count. You can wait until it lets go.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: It should only take a—no, little creature, that is my cuff. Bozhe moy.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: The cat or the count?

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: Do not be pleased with yourself.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: We ask the groundskeeper about the cat and learn that it belongs to a nearby house. It leaves through the hedge on its own.

closing.speaker: Katya
closing.text: A terrible creature.

closing.speaker: Narration
closing.text: Before we go, she checks that nobody has closed the gap in the fence.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: Class B needs a small budget for its first-year display. A classmate suggests asking Katya's father to pay.

setup.speaker: Katya
setup.text: We have a school allowance. We will work within it.

setup.speaker: Classmate
setup.text: It was just an idea.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: The classmate leaves for another assignment. Katya crosses out a cost, pressing hard enough to mark the next page.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: We could use plain backing paper.

setup.speaker: Katya
setup.text: Yes. Or fewer printed photographs.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: You don't have to solve every part before the next meeting.

setup.speaker: Katya
setup.text: Apparently I do, or somebody will solve it by calling my father.

choices.text: Let's put the cheaper options beside the expensive ones. The class can decide.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: You would let them see an unfinished proposal?

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I'd let them help finish it.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: That is... irritatingly reasonable. Start with the printing costs.

choices.text: Let's ask the teacher how much the allowance covers.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: We should confirm that before ordering anything.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I'll write down the questions.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: And I will try not to answer them all before we reach the staffroom.

choices.text: Your father could help once. It would save everyone a lot of trouble.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: Including the trouble of taking our work seriously?

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I meant the money, not your effort.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: People rarely bother to separate the two.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: The budget is small enough to understand and large enough to argue about. We make a clean copy for the class.

closing.speaker: Narration
closing.text: Katya leaves her surname off the proposal title. Every member's name goes in the credits instead.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: The library lends us a reference table. Katya has rewritten nearly the entire display plan overnight.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: There's a signature space for three people. Only yours is filled.

setup.speaker: Katya
setup.text: The other sections were incomplete.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: So you did them too?

setup.speaker: Katya
setup.text: I required a finished plan, not a lesson in patience.

setup.speaker: Narration
setup.text: She rubs her wrist, then immediately stops when she notices me looking.

setup.speaker: Katya
setup.text: I am not asking you to feel sorry for me.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: I was going to ask where the original drafts went.

choices.text: We can give everyone one last deadline.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: A specific one. Not 'whenever you have time.'

response.speaker: MC
response.text: Before the end of this block.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: At least that can be measured.

choices.text: If you want everything your way, you may as well do it all.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: I am aware of the option. I have been exercising it.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: Then why ask anyone else?

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: I begin to wonder the same thing.

choices.text: Put my section back. Tell me what's wrong with it and let me fix it.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: The image credits are missing, and the last paragraph repeats the first.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: Good. That's something I can actually fix.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: I will check it when you are finished. Once.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: We spend the block comparing drafts rather than replacing them. The final plan has three different sets of corrections.

closing.speaker: Katya
closing.text: That sentence is yours. It should stay in your voice.

closing.speaker: Narration
closing.text: Her pen hovers, then moves to the next page.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: The MC returns from an errand and hears Katya speaking Russian near the stairwell. Her usual clipped certainty has gone quiet.

setup.speaker: Katya
setup.text: Yes. I understand. I will send it when it is finished.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: She ends the call and sees the folder in the MC's hands.

setup.speaker: Katya
setup.text: How long have you been there?

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: Long enough to know I should have made more noise.

setup.speaker: Katya
setup.text: It was my mother. That is all.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: The clipped schoolroom rhythm returns, each word carefully placed. A trace of Russian still rounds the last vowel.

setup.speaker: Narration
setup.text: It clearly isn't all. It is, however, all she has offered.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: The teacher approved the cheaper paper.

choices.text: Was she disappointed in you? You sounded different.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: You have mistaken hearing a conversation for being invited into it.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I only wanted to understand.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: Then understand that I do not wish to discuss it.

choices.text: Want the folder now, or a minute first?

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: A minute would be useful.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I'll be by the noticeboard.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: Thank you. I will come over.

choices.text: I'll leave the folder on your desk.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: Very well. I will read it shortly.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: The note on top explains the changes.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: I saw. Thank you.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: Later, we attach paper samples to the display mock-up. The MC does not ask again about the call.

closing.speaker: Katya
closing.text: My mother was a dancer. She hears an unfinished plan and imagines a missed step.

closing.speaker: Narration
closing.text: She says it while measuring a margin. I keep my eyes on the ruler and let her decide whether to say more.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: A supply delivery arrives under the wrong name. Someone has written 'Romanova donation' on a school-funded box.

setup.speaker: Katya
setup.text: It is an ordinary purchase. The receipt is inside.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: We'll correct the label.

setup.speaker: Katya
setup.text: After half the class has seen it.

setup.speaker: Narration
setup.text: A classmate asks if her family bought the display equipment. Katya's reply is so formal that the conversation stops.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: We still have the order sheet.

setup.speaker: Katya
setup.text: I know. I would prefer evidence to another sympathetic speech.

choices.text: Let's attach the school receipt and explain the mistake together.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: Keep it brief.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: Wrong label, school budget, corrected record. No speech.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: An excellent length.

choices.text: The teacher can clear it up at the next meeting.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: That would be appropriate.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I'll leave the receipt with the order sheet.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: Please make a copy first.

choices.text: People will believe what they want. We might as well use the reputation.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: You think I should benefit from something that is untrue?

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I think fighting it is exhausting you.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: Then let me choose what is worth my effort.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: The incorrect label comes off. The receipt stays with the supplies, where anyone can check it.

closing.speaker: Narration
closing.text: There is no grand apology from the whole school. By the next bell, most people are discussing lunch.

closing.speaker: Katya
closing.text: You were right about one thing. They do move on quickly.

warm.speaker: Katya
warm.text: I trust you to explain your part. I would rather not speak for you.

mixed.speaker: Katya
mixed.text: Let us be clear about what we are telling people.

cool.speaker: Katya
cool.text: We can correct the purchase record. My family is not part of the discussion.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: A supervised practice match has ended. Katya loses the last point, removes her mask and thanks her opponent before speaking to anyone else.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: Want me to carry the markers back?

setup.speaker: Katya
setup.text: In a moment. I am trying to remember when my foot stopped obeying me.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: The instructor said your recovery was better.

setup.speaker: Katya
setup.text: My recovery was necessary because I made the first mistake.

setup.speaker: Narration
setup.text: She watches the empty lane as if the last point might happen again.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: Is there a version of this afternoon where you're allowed to be disappointed?

setup.speaker: Katya
setup.text: I am testing it. The results are unpleasant.

choices.text: We could ask the instructor what to work on next.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: I already have. Distance and patience.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: Hard to mark those with tape.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: A flaw in your otherwise excellent system.

choices.text: You can hate losing. You don't have to pretend the whole practice was worthless.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: I did not say the whole practice was worthless.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: You were making a strong case.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: Hm. Perhaps I was.

choices.text: It's only a school match. You're taking it too seriously.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: It matters to me. That should be enough information.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I was trying to help you forget it.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: I am trying to learn from it. Kindly allow me to be annoyed and competent at the same time.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: We reset the lane for the next group. Katya walks the movement slowly, then packs her equipment.

closing.speaker: Katya
closing.text: My opponent earned that last point.

closing.speaker: MC
closing.text: You'll tell her?

closing.speaker: Katya
closing.text: I already did. I can be unhappy without being unfair.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: The display assembly has reached the part that never appears in photographs: cutting backing card and checking every caption.

setup.speaker: Katya
setup.text: This section is still blank.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: It belongs to Sato. He's collecting the prints.

setup.speaker: Katya
setup.text: I could complete it before he returns.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: You could.

setup.speaker: Narration
setup.text: She looks at the empty space, then at the scissors already in her hand.

setup.speaker: Katya
setup.text: You are waiting for me to have a revelation, aren't you?

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: Mostly I'm waiting for the glue.

choices.text: I'll fill it in while he's gone. We don't have to tell him.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: That would be efficient.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: See? Problem solved.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: No. Put it down. I know exactly how that ends.

choices.text: Let's finish our section. We can check his when he gets back.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: And if it is late?

response.speaker: MC
response.text: Then we deal with a late section. We don't erase his part in advance.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: Fine. Pass me the glue.

choices.text: I'll message him for an update.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: Ask whether he needs help collecting them.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: That's a better question than 'Where are you?'

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: It had better produce a better answer.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: Sato returns with the prints and a reasonable explanation. Katya checks his captions without rewriting his introduction.

closing.speaker: Katya
closing.text: There. Finished.

closing.speaker: Narration
closing.text: She has done less of it herself than she intended. For once, that looks like part of the achievement.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: After the committee work, a teacher asks us to stay available in case the display needs changes. No changes arrive.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: We might be finished.

setup.speaker: Katya
setup.text: Do not say that too confidently. Work can hear you.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: She has brought a small dark-chocolate bar. She places it between us, still wrapped.

setup.speaker: Katya
setup.text: For the table. Not a reward.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: I wasn't about to put it on my report card.

setup.speaker: Katya
setup.text: Good.

setup.speaker: Narration
setup.text: Without a folder between us, the table looks unexpectedly wide.

choices.text: What would you be doing today if nobody needed anything from you?

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: Listening to music. Possibly walking somewhere without a destination.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: That sounds possible.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: An alarming thought. I had become rather attached to being too busy.

choices.text: Want to review the display once more before we leave?

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: We have checked it twice.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: Old habits.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: Apparently contagious ones. Finish your chocolate first.

choices.text: You'd probably be bored without people relying on you.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: Perhaps. I would still like to discover whether I have a personality when nobody needs a budget.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: You never seemed interested in doing nothing.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: You have rarely asked.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: We talk about music until the teacher tells us there are no more changes. Katya recommends a piano recording, then spells the title so I can find it.

closing.speaker: Katya
closing.text: You do not have to enjoy it.

closing.speaker: MC
closing.text: Good. I'd hate to fail listening homework.

closing.speaker: Katya
closing.text: There is no exam. That is the point.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: The class is submitting its display record. Katya has left the final signature space for the MC.

setup.speaker: Katya
setup.text: Read it before you sign. I am not asking for blind agreement.

setup.speaker: Narration
setup.text: The report credits the class, records the budget mistake and names the work that was corrected. It does not turn every problem into somebody else's fault.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: You left the changes in.

setup.speaker: Katya
setup.text: They happened. The first version was not the finished version.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: Sounds obvious when you say it like that.

setup.speaker: Katya
setup.text: Most difficult things do, afterwards.

choices.text: It looks accurate. I'll sign.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: Thank you. We can hand it in together.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: And finally retire the folder?

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: A dignified retirement. It has suffered enough.

choices.text: Could we leave out the mistakes? The report would sound more impressive.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: It would sound less true.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: Nobody needs every awkward detail.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: Then do not add any. But the corrections stay.

choices.text: Before I sign, I want to be honest about my part too.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: Then be specific. I can listen to specifics.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: Some days I helped. Some days I said what was easiest. I don't want the report to hide either.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: All right. We will get the wording right.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: We finish the record and leave it in the submission tray. The desk is suddenly clear.

closing.speaker: Katya
closing.text: I will be at the gate after dismissal next time. If you want to talk without a task attached.

closing.speaker: Narration
closing.text: It is an invitation to a conversation, not a promise about what she will say.

warm.speaker: Katya
warm.text: I have become accustomed to having you beside me. That is not a complaint.

mixed.speaker: Katya
mixed.text: We have managed the work. I am still deciding what to make of the rest.

cool.speaker: Katya
cool.text: There are a few things I would rather settle directly than leave unspoken.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: Finale encounter. The UI warns that completing this conversation ends the current playthrough. Katya waits at the gate, holding an ordinary convenience-store bag.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: No folder?

setup.speaker: Katya
setup.text: I considered bringing one. It would have made this less conspicuous.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: Is that melonpan?

setup.speaker: Katya
setup.text: You are very observant when bread is involved.

setup.speaker: Narration
setup.text: She has bought two. It would be easy to treat that as an answer before asking the question.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: I wanted to say something properly. I like you, Katya. More than as a classmate.

setup.speaker: Katya
setup.text: Then let us be clear about what you are asking.

choices.text: After all this time, I think I've proved I deserve a chance.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: My affection is not a prize for completing enough tasks.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: That came out wrong.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: It came out clearly. Let me finish before you explain it away.

choices.text: I'd like to go out with you. You can tell me honestly if you don't want that.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: I intended to answer honestly in any case.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I know. I wanted you to hear that I can accept it.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: Good. Then listen.

choices.text: I'm not sure what happens next. I wanted you to know how I feel.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: A statement rather than a demand. I can work with that.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: It took me a while to get the wording right.

response.speaker: Katya
response.text: I noticed.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: Record this choice once, then compare the route's total effective good and bad counts. Play exactly one ending below. Do not show a default acceptance before evaluating the score.

warm.speaker: Katya
warm.text: I was hoping you would come. No—do not look so pleased. I have not finished.

mixed.speaker: Katya
mixed.text: I am glad we can speak directly, whatever we decide.

cool.speaker: Katya
cool.text: I came because an honest conversation is better than another misunderstanding.

endings.title: No Need to Keep Up
endings.cgBrief: Katya beside the gate in soft late-afternoon light, silver hair in broad clean locks, small sincere smile, offering a wrapped melonpan; the MC is a plain charcoal silhouette at equal height beside her. No glamour framing.

lines.speaker: Katya
lines.text: I like you too. There. An entirely ordinary sentence. Apparently beyond my ordinary capabilities.

lines.speaker: MC
lines.text: You hid it better than I did.

lines.speaker: Katya
lines.text: That is a very low standard.

lines.speaker: Stage
lines.text: She gives him one of the wrapped breads. Their hands briefly touch; neither pulls the other closer.

lines.speaker: Katya
lines.text: There is a café near the station. Saturday, if you are free.

lines.speaker: MC
lines.text: A date?

lines.speaker: Katya
lines.text: Yes, Takahashi—Ren. Bozhe moy. I am attempting to eliminate ambiguity, not create more of it.

lines.speaker: MC
lines.text: Saturday works.

lines.speaker: Narration
lines.text: I used to imagine that a confession would be the moment I finally said everything perfectly. Instead, I'm smiling so hard I can barely unwrap the bread.

lines.speaker: Katya
lines.text: And if you dislike the café, say so. I have no intention of dating somebody who agrees with me out of fear.

lines.speaker: MC
lines.text: What if I disagree out of terrible taste?

lines.speaker: Katya
lines.text: We shall have to see how terrible. And don't smile like that, durak. You'll make me smile too.

lines.speaker: Stage
lines.text: She falls into step beside him. Neither of them needs to set the pace for both.

lines.speaker: Narration
lines.text: The gate closes behind us. There are ordinary things to decide now: which street to take, whether it will rain, when I can see her again. I want the chance to learn them.

lines.speaker: Stage
lines.text: Unlock Katya / Good. Return to title after credits.

endings.title: The Seat Across From Her
endings.cgBrief: A quiet Class B desk with the completed folder between two chairs; Katya offers a small cordial smile across the table. Open daytime light, respectful distance.

lines.speaker: Katya
lines.text: I value the time we have spent together. I cannot honestly call what I feel romance.

lines.speaker: MC
lines.text: All right.

lines.speaker: Katya
lines.text: You are allowed to look disappointed. I would prefer that to a very brave lie.

lines.speaker: MC
lines.text: I was hoping for a different answer. But I don't want one you have to force.

lines.speaker: Stage
lines.text: The next school day, they collect the spare display materials in Class B. Katya puts the familiar folder on the table.

lines.speaker: Katya
lines.text: Will sitting here be uncomfortable?

lines.speaker: MC
lines.text: A little, probably. Not forever.

lines.speaker: Katya
lines.text: Tell me if you need room. I can manage a direct answer.

lines.speaker: Narration
lines.text: There is no sudden trick that changes what she said. There is also no reason to pretend the afternoons meant nothing.

lines.speaker: MC
lines.text: You can still send me the name of that piano piece.

lines.speaker: Katya
lines.text: I already did. You spelled it incorrectly in your notes.

lines.speaker: MC
lines.text: Of course I did.

lines.speaker: Stage
lines.text: She smiles, small and uncomplicated, and pushes the spare scissors across the desk.

lines.speaker: Narration
lines.text: For now, I take the seat across from her. Friendship is a different answer. It is still an answer worth treating carefully.

lines.speaker: Stage
lines.text: Unlock Katya / Neutral. Return to title after credits.

endings.title: A Closed Folder
endings.cgBrief: Katya alone in Class B in cool late light, calmly closing the completed folder; second chair empty, her expression disappointed but steady. No tears as spectacle.

lines.speaker: Katya
lines.text: I do not want to date you. I also think we need some distance.

lines.speaker: MC
lines.text: Because of what I just said?

lines.speaker: Katya
lines.text: Because of more than one afternoon. I have tried to tell you when something mattered to me. Too often, you treated it as something to get around.

lines.speaker: Narration
lines.text: I start preparing an explanation. Hearing it in my head, I realize it would be another request for her to make this easier for me.

lines.speaker: MC
lines.text: I heard you. I won't keep asking.

lines.speaker: Katya
lines.text: Thank you.

lines.speaker: Stage
lines.text: The next day, the MC collects his remaining papers from Class B. Katya closes the committee folder and puts it with the finished work.

lines.speaker: Katya
lines.text: Your section is in the copy on the left. You should keep it.

lines.speaker: MC
lines.text: Right. Thank you for working with me.

lines.speaker: Katya
lines.text: We did finish it.

lines.speaker: Narration
lines.text: The empty chair does not accuse me. It is simply empty. She is allowed to decide who sits beside her, and I do not get to turn that into another test of her kindness.

lines.speaker: Stage
lines.text: He takes his papers and leaves. She returns to her own plans.

lines.speaker: Narration
lines.text: Next time I care about somebody, I want to listen before I'm afraid of losing them.

lines.speaker: Stage
lines.text: Unlock Katya / Bad. Return to title after credits.

lines.speaker: MC
lines.text: Wait. Saying I deserved a chance was unfair. You don't owe me a date. I'm sorry.

lines.speaker: Katya
lines.text: Good. I would rather not begin anything with an invoice attached. I know you can listen; do so now.
